title: Python SDK: parse shims for typed models + retry ergonomics for streaming responses
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a lightweight compatibility layer (parse shims) and a set of ergonomic retry patterns for the Python SDK to make typed models (pydantic/dataclasses) reliable when consumed from streaming generation endpoints. Goal: users should be able to declare response models and reliably hydrate incremental chunks into working model instances without surprising validation errors during retries or partial reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming parse shim transforms incremental JSON chunks into stable pydantic/dataclass objects with clear error semantics
Retryable stream reconnect preserves already-hydrated fields and resumes parsing without duplicating results
Comprehensive unit tests (>= 80% coverage for shim + retry logic) and integration tests against the local runtimes mock
Examples added to SDK cookbook: one for dataclass + backoff-aware streaming, one for pydantic + graceful-fallback
Performance: shim adds <5% median latency overhead vs raw stream parse in our benchmark harness
Docs updated: migration guide for users of existing streaming helpers and changelog entry with default behaviors
steps: Design: draft spec for stream parse state machine and retry semantics (owned by @Marco)
Prototype: implement parse shims that buffer partial JSON frames and validate incrementally
Retries: implement idempotent resume by attaching a durable chunk cursor and dedupe logic
API: expose two helper primitives: stream_to_model_iter(stream, model_cls, strict=False) and RobustStreamReader(stream, resume_token=None)
Testing: unit tests for edge cases (malformed chunk boundary, repeated chunk on reconnect, missing fields), add integration test against local mock server
Docs & examples: add cookbook recipes and a migration note in SDK release notes
Review & rollout: internal review, dogfood in Redwood Console feature branch, feature-flagged rollout
notes: 2026-02-26: Kickoff meeting — consensus to keep defaults conservative (strict parsing off by default) to avoid breaking existing customers
2026-03-01: Spike showed two practical approaches: incremental-validate-on-field vs final-assemble-then-validate. Chose incremental-validate for faster failure modes and better developer feedback
2026-03-04: Design review feedback from Leah Chen — add explicit resume_token in protocol and surface simple backoff helper in public API
2026-03-08: Performance bench against local mock: incremental parsing adds ~2.7% median CPU overhead on small payloads (within target)
2026-03-10: PR opened (WIP) with core shim + tests; needs docs and integration test before merge
tradeoffs: Incremental validation surfaces errors earlier but requires holding partial model state and may reject temporarily-invalid intermediate representations
Keeping strict=False by default preserves compatibility but can hide subtle schema drift; documented opt-in strict mode will catch drift sooner
Resume via resume_token relies on server-provided stable chunk ids — if upstream cannot provide stable cursors, fallback dedupe heuristics will be used (best-effort)
implementation_notes: Prototype includes small state machine: BUFFER -> EMIT_FIELD -> VALIDATE_FIELD -> COMMIT. Uses fastjson or orjson where available. Exposes opt-in strict mode (raises ValidationError on first invalid chunk) and lenient mode (buffers until complete). Backoff uses jittered exponential with default max_retries=5.
qa_plan: Unit tests for parse state transitions and malformed chunk boundaries
Integration test running against local runtime mock that simulates reconnects and duplicate chunks
Canary dogfood: enable new helpers for internal Console ingest for 1 week, monitor error spikes and latency
Post-release: add telemetry event for shim usage and success/failure rates
